Do you want to build high-performance e-commerce solutions that connect millions of customers with sustainable water technology? Join our mission to pioneer smarter water solutions that reduce energy use and improve lives  and be partof building high-performance digital solutions that connect customers around the world and create simpler, smarter and more seamless buying experiences.

As our new Senior Software Developer – SAP Commerce, you'll develop and maintain scalable SAP Commerce and PCM solutions that power Grundfos's digital customer experience. You'll join a diverse, supportive, and inclusive culture that celebrates differences and puts people first through growth, well-being, and a strong sense of belonging.

What you will be doing

As part of the eCommerce team, you’ll help shape and deliver high-performing eCommerce solutions for customers worldwide. You’ll also work closely with the Catalogue team, contributing your expertise to SAP PCM and helping ensure strong product data capabilities across our digital solutions.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Developing high-quality software solutions using Java, Spring, and SAP Commerce (Hybris) in an agile setup

• Acting as the team's SAP PCM subject matter expert, ensuring high-quality product data across eCommerce and Catalogue solutions

• Collaborating with Product Owners, Architects, and Business Consultants to translate business needs into robust technical solutions

• Participating in design and code reviews to maintain quality standards and development best practices

• Mentoring developers and contributing to technical and architectural decisions

• Working closely with Product and Agile Delivery Leads to deliver high-quality solutions through modern CI/CD pipelines

What makes you a great fit

Above all, you're a skilled Java developer with deep SAP Commerce expertise, strong collaboration skills, and a passion for sharing knowledge and supporting colleagues. We'd also imagine that you have:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience in Java and Spring-based software development

• Hands-on experience with SAP CX, particularly SAP Commerce (Hybris)

• Strong understanding of software design principles, development best practices, and CI/CD processes

It's a plus if you also have:

• Experience with cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud Platform

• Experience integrating third-party solutions such as marketplaces, payment service providers, ERP, or CRM systems

• Knowledge of SQL, database modelling, and performance optimisation

Why you'll love working here

Day to day, you can look forward to:

• A flexible working environment with home working opportunities, flexible hours, and parental support

• Annual bonuses, health insurance, and a strong focus on well-being

• Three additional paid volunteering days each year

• On-demand learning and structured development programmes to support your growth

Valuing our differences helps us see possibilities where others can't. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all abilities, experiences, and backgrounds. As part of our commitment to a safe and compliant hiring process, final candidates may be required to undergo a background check, subject to applicable local laws and regulations.

Join Grundfos, apply today!

Technical Sales Manager, Industrial Solutions, Denmark & Southern Sweden

• Are you a self-driven, ambitious sales professional who is always looking for new business opportunities and ways to make a difference for your customers?

• Do you want to become part of our Nordic Industrial Solutions team, where technical expertise, entrepreneurship, and close customer partnerships are at the heart of everything we do?

If so, this position at Alsiano might be the perfect match for you!

About Alsiano

For more than 65 years, Alsiano has partnered with leading international manufacturers of raw materials and additives. We specialize in raw materials and additives for industrial applications such as plastics and elastomers, paints and coatings, industrial and institutional (I&I) cleaning products, household cleaning products, food, and healthcare.

The Role

You will be responsible for your customer portfolio in Denmark and Southern Sweden, where you will offer plastic raw materials and additives. Your focus will be on growing your existing customer base while identifying new customers and business opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

• Conduct customer visits to identify potential and explore new business opportunities, prepare offers, negotiate prices, and follow up on projects and sales pipelines.

• Deliver technical product presentations and solution recommendations during customer meetings.

• Participate in relevant webinars, exhibitions, seminars, and other customer-related events.

• Proactively plan and manage your sales activities in a structured manner.

• Collaborate closely with key suppliers and identify opportunities for new supplier partnerships by recognizing market trends and customer needs.

You will independently drive the entire sales process, from building and managing your pipeline to arranging meetings and preparing offers. A significant portion of your time will involve customer visits and communication via webinars, phone, and other channels.

You will analyze customer needs, objectives, challenges, and opportunities, advising customers on how Alsiano's solutions can positively impact their products and business. In close collaboration with suppliers and colleagues, you will develop tailored solutions and successfully convert opportunities into sales.

Who You Are

To succeed in this role, we expect you to have at least 3-5 years’ experience in technical B2B sales, combined with a relevant technical education. It is essential that you can effectively engage with customers, work independently, and bring a high level of energy and self-motivation.

You possess excellent negotiation and communication skills in Danish and English and have a good understanding of Swedish. Experience selling plastic raw materials to industrial customers is a distinct advantage.

Furthermore, you are:

• An ambitious and professional trusted advisor who delivers a high level of customer service.

• Able to balance both short-term and long-term objectives and prioritize your efforts accordingly.

• Results-oriented and motivated to achieve ambitious goals.

• Energetic, flexible, outgoing, and systematic in your approach.

• Quality-conscious with a strong attention to detail.

What We Offer

You will be part of a well-functioning Nordic Industrial Solutions team, where you work closely with colleagues across the Nordic region and report directly to the Head of Nordic Sales, Industrial Solutions, based in Gothenburg.

This is a challenging role in a collaborative and supportive environment, where we help each other grow, develop, and create value. We offer a flexible work environment, allowing you to work from Alsiano’s office in Birkerød or from home.

The position involves travel, primarily within Denmark and Southern Sweden, as well as occasional travel to other European countries, approximately 60-80 days per year.

Click "Apply" and upload your CV.

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

Our IoT team builds the devices and edge software that connect our customers' production lines to the Factbird platform, from sensors on the line to industrial edge computers running computer vision right next to the machines. We're a small team with broad ownership, and we're hiring an Embedded Platform Engineer to help build and run the platform our edge products stand on.

**This role is onsite in Copenhagen, Denmark. We welcome applications from candidates based in Spain who are open to relocating to Copenhagen.

**

About the Role

As Embedded Platform Engineer, you'll work hands-on across Factbird EDGE, our industrial edge platform, together with the rest of the IoT team: the operating system, the device software, and the vision models that run on it. You'll take ownership of the infrastructure around the devices: provisioning and recovery, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability, the systems that keep our unattended devices reliable, secure, and safely updatable in factories you may never visit.

You'll work in Rust on embedded Linux, with Yocto, AWS IoT Greengrass, GStreamer and ONNX Runtime at the core, alongside our Cloud and DevOps engineers and the people building our AI capabilities. Part of the job is shaping the role with the team as our edge products grow.

You'll thrive here if you like working across a system end to end, from the bootloader to the cloud connection, and if you'd rather fix the root cause in the build than patch around it on the device.

What you'll do

Embedded Linux & the EDGE platform

• Develop our Yocto-based Linux distribution: layers, BSPs, kernel configuration, and reproducible builds

• Build and maintain the Rust components that run on our edge devices

• Bring up new hardware platforms, debug on target, and keep the platform secure and maintainable over a long device lifetime

• Keep our CI and on-hardware testing healthy, so changes reach devices with confidence

Edge inference & vision

• Work with our ML and vision engineers on the device side of our computer vision capabilities: camera pipelines, video streaming, and model inference that runs efficiently on industrial hardware

• Share ownership with our ML engineers of how trained models move from our model pipeline onto devices and how they perform there: packaging, rollout, rollback, and drift monitoring

• Help bring new edge runtimes for vision workloads from development into production

Fleet infrastructure & ownership

• Own device provisioning, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability

• Make deployments to devices in the field safe and boring: staged rollouts, health checks, and recovery paths

• Help diagnose issues on devices at customer sites, working with Support, Product, and Cloud to turn them into lasting fixes

• Share knowledge in both directions: learn the parts of the platform others built, and make sure what you build doesn't live only in your head

**What we're looking for

**

We're looking for an engineer who has shipped embedded Linux into production and lived with it afterwards: someone who has debugged a device they couldn't touch, and who wants real responsibility rather than a ticket queue.

You work independently, but you don't work alone. You can take a loosely defined problem and move it forward without daily direction, and you pull others in early, because on a small team the best fix is one more than one person understands. You're disciplined where it matters, in releases and rollouts, and curious where it pays off, in vision and new hardware.

You don't need everything below. Yocto is the core. Rust matters, but strong C/C++ engineers who have started with Rust are welcome too. The rest you can grow into with us.

**

The ideal background**

• Hands-on experience shipping embedded Linux to production, including Yocto: layers, BSPs and images you've built and maintained yourself, not just consumed

• Strong systems programming in Rust, or deep C/C++ experience on embedded Linux and real exposure to Rust that you want to build on

• An advantage if you have worked with AWS IoT Core or Greengrass, video pipelines or ML inference on edge hardware, or in industrial settings where devices run unattended for years

• A solid grasp of embedded security and update mechanisms: signed images, A/B or similar update schemes, and secure device provisioning

• You can explain a technical trade-off clearly, whether you're talking to another engineer, Support or a customer, and you do it in fluent English

• We welcome applications from people eager to move to Denmark, as long as you already have the legal right to live and work here.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We'd love to hear from you

**

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at **crva@factbird.com

About Factbird

Great people make great things happen

Factbird is on a mission to make manufacturing more efficient. We build intuitive tools that give frontline teams the insights they need to reduce waste, improve processes, and stay ahead. Since 2016, we’ve helped manufacturers worldwide drive real change. Now, we’re searching for great people to help us do even more.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is an advanced systems and industrialization company developing integrated technology platforms for demanding aerospace, security, and mission-critical applications. Its mission is to transform operationally validated technologies into scalable, ready-to-deploy systems by combining advanced engineering, industrial partnerships, and strong governance.

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development. The site will build core capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, industrialization, and deployment of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be an advanced aerospace signal-intelligence product platform covering RF and system architecture, antenna-system design, RF and microwave hardware, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for qualification, production, and operational deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and international deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s mechanical design capability for antenna and RF systems. The role is intended for an experienced mechanical engineer with prior hands-on experience developing the mechanical implementation of antenna, RF, or microwave hardware.

You will design and develop mechanical solutions for antenna systems and associated RF and electronic assemblies. The work includes antenna supports and mounts, RF-aware enclosures, radomes, fixed and, where applicable, deployable antenna mechanisms, test fixtures, thermal solutions, connector integration, cable routing, sealing, environmental protection, and platform interfaces. Many of these structures can directly affect antenna and RF performance, requiring close co-design with antenna and RF engineers.

The role covers mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing-process selection, structural and thermal analysis, tolerance definition, detailed CAD design, prototyping, assembly, environmental validation, serviceability, and production release. Particular attention will be given to mechanical structures that directly affect antenna performance, integration, alignment, stability, and deployment.

You will work closely with antenna systems engineers, RF and microwave hardware engineers, system architects, RF test and characterization engineers, manufacturing partners, and partner engineering teams. The role requires strong mechanical design expertise, RF-aware product thinking, end-to-end technical ownership, and hands-on implementation experience, taking designs from concept through prototype build and qualification to documented, manufacturable antenna assemblies and integrated systems.

Key responsibilities

• Translate system, antenna, and platform requirements into mechanical architectures, interface definitions, design constraints, and technical trade-offs.

• Design mechanical components and assemblies for antenna systems, including supports, mounts, frames, radomes, RF-aware enclosures, fixed or deployable mechanisms, and platform-integration structures.

• Own the detailed mechanical implementation of antenna and RF assemblies, including 3D CAD models, 2D manufacturing drawings, GD&T, assembly-level tolerance analysis, BOMs, and configuration-controlled documentation.

• Develop mechanical solutions that maintain antenna alignment, dimensional stability, RF clearances, grounding, shielding, cable routing, connector accessibility, and other mechanical conditions required to achieve the intended electromagnetic performance.

• Integrate RF modules, antennas, electronics, connectors, cables, gaskets, thermal interfaces, and environmental sealing into complete mechanical assemblies.

• Perform structural, thermal, and tolerance analyses covering stiffness, strength, mass properties, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, and expected environmental loads.

• Define mechanical requirements and work jointly with antenna and RF engineers to establish electromagnetic constraints for radomes, covers, supports, enclosures, and other structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Design antenna deployment and positioning mechanisms, where applicable, including hinges, latches, restraints, stops, alignment features, and associated interfaces.

• Design test fixtures, alignment tools, handling aids, assembly tooling, and prototype-support hardware for antenna and RF system development.

• Select materials, coatings, surface treatments, fasteners, adhesives, seals, bearings, and manufacturing processes based on structural, thermal, RF, environmental, corrosion, and production requirements.

• Lead mechanical prototype build, assembly, troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Contribute to environmental testing and qualification, including vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, and other relevant mechanical validation activities.

• Apply design-for-manufacture, design-for-assembly, serviceability, reliability, and cost considerations throughout development.

• Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners on technical clarification, process selection, prototype production, inspection, non-conformance resolution, and production release.

• Prepare mechanical specifications, analysis reports, interface-control documentation, design-review materials, assembly instructions, and production handover documentation.

• Collaborate with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and engineering workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

Required qualifications and experience

• Degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

• 5+ years of professional mechanical design experience, including demonstrated experience developing mechanical hardware for antenna, RF, or microwave systems where mechanical geometry, materials, interfaces, tolerances, or nearby structures directly influence electromagnetic performance.

• Strong hands-on experience and demonstrated technical ownership of complex mechanical assemblies from initial architecture and concept through detailed design, prototype build, verification, qualification, and production release.

• Advanced proficiency with a professional 3D CAD and drafting environment; SolidWorks experience is preferred.

• Strong command of GD&T, engineering drawing standards, assembly-level tolerance analysis, and production-quality mechanical documentation.

• Demonstrated experience designing mechanical components or assemblies for antenna, RF, or microwave systems, such as antenna supports and mounts, frames, enclosures, radomes, mechanisms, fixtures, or other mechanically and electromagnetically constrained structures.

• Experience with mechanical packaging and integration of antennas, RF modules, PCBs, connectors, cables, thermal interfaces, shielding, grounding, seals, and associated electronics.

• Practical understanding of RF-aware mechanical design, including the effects of materials, structures, clearances, alignment, grounding, shielding, cabling, and radomes on antenna and RF performance.

• Experience applying engineering calculations and simulation methods, including finite-element analysis where appropriate, to support structural and thermal design decisions.

• Understanding of stiffness, strength, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, fatigue, and other relevant environmental loads.

• Practical knowledge of metallic materials, engineering polymers, elastomers, composites, adhesives, coatings, and surface treatments.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, such as precision machining, sheet-metal fabrication, additive manufacturing, composite manufacturing, joining, fastening, sealing, and assembly.

• Demonstrated hands-on experience with prototype assembly, mechanical troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Experience supporting environmental testing and qualification, such as vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, or comparable validation activities.

• Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing teams on process selection, technical clarification, inspection, non-conformance resolution, manufacturability, and production handover.

Nice to have

• Experience developing lightweight, stiffness-critical structures with stringent alignment and dimensional-stability requirements.

• Experience with aerospace or space-hardware qualification, including thermal-vacuum testing, outgassing constraints, vibration, and shock.

• Experience with precision mechanical alignment, dimensional inspection, antenna positioning, and calibration or verification fixtures.

• Experience designing IP-rated enclosures or ruggedized outdoor electronic equipment.

• Experience with product data management, configuration control, and release processes for complex mechanical assemblies.

• Experience working with international suppliers and manufacturing partners on low-volume, high-complexity hardware.

• Experience designing radomes, RF-transparent structures, or mechanical structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Experience with mechanically steerable, deployable, foldable, or position-critical antenna systems.

• Experience working directly with antenna or electromagnetic simulation engineers to iterate mechanical geometry, materials, and interfaces based on RF performance.

Success in the first 6 months

• Take end-to-end technical ownership of one or more mechanical subsystems or integration areas for antenna and RF systems.

• Establish the initial mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing approach, and platform-integration plan for the assigned scope.

• Deliver reviewed 3D models, manufacturing drawings, tolerance analyses, interface definitions, and supporting design documentation.

• Develop and support the build, assembly, and verification of initial mechanical prototypes, fixtures, or engineering models.

• Identify key structural, thermal, alignment, sealing, deployment, and manufacturability risks and define practical mitigation actions.

• Establish effective technical interfaces with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, supplier, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and release workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

Would you like to join the Regulatory Report team in Reporting Solutions, responsible for several critical business solutions and reporting processes within Credit and Financial Risk? Do you want to participate in the data tech transformation in BEC, soon to be Nykredit Financial Technologies?

BEC is looking for a Senior Business Analyst to join the Reporting Solutions domain. The position will be based at our friendly office in Roskilde or Warsaw.

Reporting Solutions plays a vital role in ensuring compliance of BEC’s member banks by managing a portfolio of 40+ business solutions within the business areas of Credit Risk and Finance Solutions, including several business-critical data hubs that support banks' business processes, internal reporting, and obligations in regulatory reporting.

You will join the Regulatory Reporting team with responsibility for both maintenance and development of a portfolio of business solutions that ensure accurate, reliable, and traceable data for our Credit Risk - Standardized Approach (SA-CR) provided by NASDAQ (Axiom), Unlikeliness to Pay, ESG and other applications within Regulatory Reporting.

You will join a high‑performing, cross‑functional team, combining solid business knowledge with strong software engineering practices. The team works with NASDAQ Axiom, Mainframe, Netezza, and Databricks platforms. The team is currently situated in Herning but will transition and consolidate in Roskilde and Warsaw by end of 2027.

This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of BEC’s data tech transformation, using modern, Cloud-based technologies and event‑driven architectures to build scalable data products to substitute for current business solutions. This will give banks easier access to trusted, consistent data, whether for self-service analytics, reporting, regulatory requirements, or operational processes.

**Primary tasks and responsibilities include:

**

• Manage incidents and problems effectively in close collaboration with colleagues and clients

• Explore and analyse complex credit risk datasets to identify patterns, anomalies, and opportunities. for improvement of business solutions and reporting processes

• Translate business and regulatory requirements into analytical use cases and communicate insights to stakeholders both internally in BEC and clients

• Collaborate closely with Business Analysts, Software Engineers, and Architects in Reporting Solutions to ensure high-quality, reliable, and well‑governed data foundations

• Build analytical data products and models that support regulatory reporting and decision‑making across the credit risk domain

• Participate in the tech and data transformation in BEC towards a modern data platform using Azure and Databricks

• Contribute to continuous improvement of the development process and client engagement

**To succeed you will have:

**

• 5+ years’ work experience as Business Analyst from Banking or financial IT

• Regulatory work experience from the banking sector in Denmark

• Extensive knowledge of the regulations: BASEL III, COREP (SA-CR), ESG, FINREP and other Regulatory reports

• Extensive experience working with large and complex datasets

• Understanding of data modelling concepts and data governance principles

• Experience of working in agile setups like Scrum or SAFe.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

• Fluency in Danish and English, written and spoken.

**It’s nice-to-have:

**

• A relevant Master degree

• Working experience with NASDAQ Axiom platform

• Programming skills in SQL, Python or Power BI

• Work experience with modern platforms such as Databricks.

As a person, you are ambitious, goal oriented, and persistent. You have a curious and analytical mindset. You are a team player who is proactive and takes responsibility. You are service minded towards both clients and colleagues.

**Be your best self with BEC's benefits!

**We offer a diverse range of benefits for our employees. Here are just a few of them.

• Professional development budget

• Healthy, varied lunch and fruit in the canteen

• Active staff associations: yoga, cycling, go-karting, games, bowling etc.

• Pension scheme

• Health and dentist insurance

• Referral bonus

**What does the recruitment process look like?

**

• Send us your CV: We want to get to know you

• Screening call: Let's chat and see if we're a match

• Meet your future manager and team: See who you'll be working closely with.

• Personality and cognitive test: Let's learn more about you.

• Meet our talent partner and your future manager once more: Get feedback on your test results.

• Time to sign the contract: We're ready to welcome you to BEC!

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Talent Attraction Partner Anders Rud Skak-Arnstrup at rud@bec.dk

BEC is in the process of being acquired by our largest customer and co-owner, Nykredit, which is Denmark's largest mortgage provider and third-largest bank. We will become part of a new and larger organization called Nykredit Financial Technologies. In the transition phase, we are recruiting for roles that we expect to be highly needed in our future organization.

Why we are hiring

Spirii is growing. We work with charge point operators, businesses and fleets in several European markets, we take part in more and more tenders, and our commercial team has grown along the way. With growth comes friction. Deals and tenders are tracked in different places, the numbers in the CRM do not always match what we bill, and it takes too much effort to answer simple questions like “what will we close this quarter?”

We want one person to own the engine behind our revenue: the CRM, the data, and the path a customer takes from first contact to signed deal, onboarding and correct billing. That is this role. You will make work easier for our sales, marketing, onboarding and customer success teams, and you will give leadership numbers they can trust.

The team

You will report to our CSO. You will own Revenue Operations from end to end, and you will work every day with sales development, account executives, marketing, onboarding and customer success, and closely with Finance on billing data.

What you will do

CRM and tools

• Own and improve HubSpot, our CRM, so everyone works from the same clean data

• Make sure every deal and tender is tracked in one place, from first contact to result

• Set up and improve lead routing

• Bring in the other tools the commercial team needs, such as order management, bid management and lead development

• Make sure master data is correct, so billing runs smoothly

Metrics and forecasting

• Define and track our core SaaS metrics: ARR, ACV, TCV, NRR and pipeline stages

• Run the weekly forecast and track how accurate it is

• Connect marketing, sales development, account executives and customer success, so the forecast reflects what is really happening

Data and reporting

• Build dashboards that leadership trusts and uses to make decisions

• Keep the CRM clean and reconcile it with billing data

Planning and sales process

• Build one clear sales process, with the same stages and rules from lead to handover across teams and markets

• Support territory design and regional planning reviews

• Run capacity modelling and lead quota planning

• Improve the path from lead to opportunity

What success looks like after your first year

• Leadership opens one dashboard and trusts what it sees

• Every deal and tender lives in HubSpot, and CRM data matches billing data

• The weekly forecast is a habit, and it gets more accurate over time

• Every market follows the same sales process

• Our sales team spends less time on admin and more time with customers

What you bring

• 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations or commercial analytics in a B2B SaaS company

• Strong CRM administration skills, ideally in HubSpot

• A track record of building tools and processes that help a sales organisation work better

• Comfort with data: Excel, SQL, or BI tools such as Tableau

• A good understanding of SaaS business models and unit economics

• Hands-on experience bringing AI tools into a sales or marketing team

• Fluent English. Another European language, such as German, French, Dutch, Swedish, Danish or Italian, is a big plus

• A degree in business, engineering or a similar field, or equivalent experience

Who you are

• You enjoy building things from the ground up, and you are comfortable when not everything is defined yet

• You take ownership and follow through

• You can think big picture and still roll up your sleeves to fix a workflow yourself

• You explain data clearly, whether you are talking to a sales rep or to the leadership team

• You like working with people from many countries and cultures

Benefits

It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but Fluent English language skills are required.

Ready to take the next step in your Risk Management career?

Do you have a natural flair for numbers and strong analytical skills? Are you ready to develop your commercial understanding of the dynamic fuel and shipping industry that facilitates global trade? As an in-house Risk Management Analyst, you will help our customers mitigate risks and navigate uncertainty and volatility. Strong relationships and stakeholder management will be central to how you create that value.

Job description

Monjasa is a leading global partner in the oil and shipping industry who believes strongly in driving Personal Business. We aim to inspire our business partners and become first choice by challenging status quo with our original solutions. We are on the lookout to expand the Risk Management team with a colleague who can identify with Monjasa’s values and can build strong relations both internally and externally.

In this role, you will work closely with Trading to propose fixed forward prices for physical bunker sales. You will define the hedging requirements and coordinate with our Derivatives team to manage the associated risk. The Derivatives team executes the paper hedges.

You will be based at our office in Fredericia and report directly to the Group Treasury and Risk Management Senior Manager. During onboarding, you will spend time with your team at our Hellerup office to build your functional knowledge and relationships. For approximately two months, you can expect three travel days to Hellerup per week.

Your role will develop quickly: you will first learn about our business activities and products, the mechanics of risk management, and pricing and hedging on live deals. As you build this foundation, you will progress towards more independent responsibility for quoting, hedge coordination and post-trade follow-up.

What you will be doing

• Act as the go-to person for traders on fixed vs. floating pricing requests, with fast and accurate turnaround

• Work side by side with other Risk Management colleagues to provide Trading with fixed forward prices

• Identify and mitigate risks inherent with fixed forward prices

• Define the hedging requirements for each deal, including the index, volume and tenor, and coordinate with the Derivatives team, which executes the paper trades

• Monitor basis risk—the risk arising from differences between physical pricing and the paper index—and flag when hedges no longer match the physical position

• Follow physical liftings, delivery shifts and volume changes, and propose the resulting hedge adjustments or unwinds

• Track PnL against realized outcome, and give feedback on pricing accuracy after delivery

• Analyze forward curves, spreads and volatility to provide insights with Global Trading teams

• Build and maintain pricing and risk tools in Excel and dashboards, and contribute to ad-hoc projects on pricing policy and process improvement

What we are looking for

Professional skills

jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for an exciting two-year postdoctoral position in the field of quantitative genetics and genomics applied to inbreeding management in livestock populations. The primary focus of this position is to investigate the genetic bases of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position starting on 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible. 

Job description
This is an opportunity to integrate a top research environment and contribute to advancing the state of the art in inbreeding management, while working within a collaborative project involving key industry partners.

The overarching objective of the project is to quantify the impact of inbreeding depression load on economically important traits in dairy cattle breeds and to investigate whether recessive variants contributing to inbreeding depression segregate in genomic regions experiencing rapid accumulation of inbreeding. Particular attention will be given to regions surrounding monogenetic traits (e.g. polled locus, milk caseins) which have been subjected to strong selection pressure in recent years.

You will apply state-of-the-art quantitative genetic and genomic modelling approaches to evaluate the effect of inbreeding depression on a broad range of production and functional traits recorded in dairy cattle populations. To support these analyses, you will have access to extensive databases containing phenotypic records routinely collected on farm, as well as large-scale pedigree and SNP genomic datasets currently used in genomic evaluations. High-density SNP genotyping and whole-genome sequence data will also be available to search for causal variants and more finely describe the genetic architecture of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle. Ultimately, the project aims to incorporate these findings into practical mating software readily available to dairy farmers. Therefore, these activities will be carried out in close collaboration with industry partners to ensure practical implementation in the field. 

Within this position, the successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects related to genetic diversity management and quantitative trait modelling across other livestock species. 

Your profile
• A Ph.D. in Quantitative Genetics, Population Genetics or similar.
• Good programming skills (R, Python or Julia)
• Experience in the use of software to estimate variance components is a plus (e.g. DMU, BLUPF90 or similar) 
• A team player and a good communicator
• A good track record of publication in international peer-reviewed journals
• Fluent in English (written and spoken)
Who we are
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and genomics at Aarhus University (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). We conduct basic and applied research in animal, plant, and human genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. Research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development and application on practical problems across species, in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strives for an excellent working environment, in which we value self-leadership, open communication, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

• A healthy work-life balance.

All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant at Department of Agroecology, Aarhus University
jobs.description:
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is offering a research assistant position to support experimental biogeochemical research, starting 01-03-2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position will be available for a 1-year period.

You will be part of an international team at Land-CRAFT, where we focus on understanding and mapping carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling in agricultural landscapes and the associated emissions of nitrous oxide, changes in ecosystem C and N stocks, and leaching of nitrate to streams and groundwaters. You will be involved in field and laboratory experiments, as well as data analysis and interpretation. We also expect you will assist in conducting preparatory background research, including thematic literature reviews on focus areas of our various projects.

We expect that you will be an important part of the research environment and that you will contribute positively to the social working environment. 

Your profile

We expect that 

• You have an MSc degree in Agrobiology, Environmental Science, Chemistry or similar.
• You have experience in using gas analyzers for the purpose of measurement of GHG fluxes.
• You have experience in planning and conducting laboratory work, including analyzing physical and chemical soil properties
• You have experience in the analysis of experimental datasets, including preparation of figures and tables
• You have solid English skills, and you thrive in an inclusive multi-cultural and diverse working environment
• You have collaborative skills and ability to take initiative.
• You are motivated by working on projects, where the overall aim is to support the green transition in agriculture
Additional qualifications

Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

• A driver’s license will be needed in order to drive to experimental sites

Who we are

We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. What we offer

Living and working in Denmark

• Five weeks of paid holiday per year.
• Generous parental leave – up to 52 weeks shared between parents, with full or partial salary.
Place of Work

The place of work is Aarhus University, Ole Worms Alle 3, Aarhus C. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

More information can be obtained from Prof. Claire Treat (claire.treat@agro.au.dk).

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions, jointly at the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed
jobs.employer_name: KU- SCIENCE - CHEM og MATH og NBI-HCØ
jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen  The Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applications for a PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions. The fellowship is shared between the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and is advertised at the Faculty of Science together with a three-year assistant professor position in causal inference at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences.

  The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.  We are willing to accommodate the successful candidate’s situation, and the exact date is a matter of agreement.

  The setup: one project, two centres  You will be supervised by Sebastian Weichwald (Associate Professor at MATH, Copenhagen Causality Lab, and causality co-lead at the Pioneer Centre for AI) and Erin Gabriel (Professor at the Department of Public Health, causality theme lead and co-director of SMARTBiomed), and work closely with the assistant professor hired at Public Health also working jointly at the two centers, so that the link between the centres runs through daily work, not only meetings.

  Causal inference is a theme both centres share and approach from two sides. This position is for someone who wants both.

  About the centres: The Pioneer Centre for AI (https://www.aicentre.dk/), hosted by the Department of Computer Science with partners across Danish universities, does fundamental AI research. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed (https://smartbiomed.dk/) develops statistical and computational methods for large-scale biomedical data to improve the treatment and prevention of disease.

  The project  In diabetes management, continuous glucose monitoring is a high-frequency biomarker that is often used in treatment decisions. Given the huge amount of information summaries must be used; differences in summaries can lead to different decisions from the same raw data.  Treatment and prevention decisions increasingly rest on high-dimensional or high-frequency patient data such as biomarkers, wearable-device streams, omics profiles and longitudinal health records. In practice these are reduced to scores, coarser summaries, learned representations or patient states before a decision is made. The project asks when such a reduced representation still supports choosing between interventions, what is lost when it does not, and how representations can be learned with the decision in mind. It starts with the decision and works backwards to the measurements, transformations and assumptions that decision needs. This project aims to answer some of these questions in general, and to provide specific solutions In diabetes management.

  Who are we looking for?  The key requirement is competence: a master’s-level background with a high level of mathematical and computational training, for example from studies in statistics, mathematics, computer science or a nearby field, and an interest in causal inference. You should be interested in biomedical applications, ideally with some prior exposure through a thesis, a project, an internship or a collaboration, and willing to talk to and learn from clinicians and biomedical researchers about the context in which the methods will be used. Programming skills and willingness to turn methods into reusable software are expected.

   

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members, around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website https://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. statistics, mathematics, or computer science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant with the help of the supervisor.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme

  To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Responsibilities and tasks:

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teach and carry out knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at internationally recognized journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project 	
• Take part in the activities of both Pioneer Centres and spend time in both research environments   We are looking for candidates with the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project, in particular a strong foundation in probability, statistics and/or machine learning at advanced master’s level 	
• Interest in and some exposure to biomedical applications, and willingness to work with clinicians and biomedical researchers 	
• Evidence of research ability in any form: a master’s thesis, a project, an internship or open-source work counts as much as a preprint; prior publications are not required 	
• Programming skills and interest in producing reusable, open software 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics and its applications 	
• Good English skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Motivation letter (approximately 1.5 pages)
 	Propose your own angle on the project and argue how it fits the two groups and the wider network, including the Pioneer Centre for AI and SMARTBiomed. Tell us why this joint setup: what you expect from working across both groups that you would not get from either side alone or from an industrial machine learning lab, and how your background prepares you for it, including any experience with biomedical or other applied collaborations. 	
• Curriculum vitae (max. two pages) including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• About you (max. one page, in prose). Tell us about the thing you are most proud of. We do not mean grades or prizes, but something you made or worked out: a report that was never published, a tool, a result, a course or side project. Say what it is and why it matters to you. Use the rest of the page for anything else you want us to know: people you have worked with, circumstances we should take into account when reading your CV, or context that does not fit a CV. 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.   How we assess

  We shortlist on the written application as a whole, weighing motivation and fit with the joint setup, the mathematical and statistical foundation relevant to the project, evidence of research ability in any form, and interest in biomedical applications. Publications are neither required nor an assessment criterion, and we do not rank applicants by the reputation of their previous institution. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Interviews may span several conversations, e.g. a technical follow-up and a conversation with the leadership of both centres. As part of this we may ask you to give a short technical presentation on a topic of your choosing, or for a sample of your work. What matters to us there is whether we can discuss science together and how we would work with each other.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Application deadline

  The deadline for applications is 5 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process

  After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  An assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the supervisors: Sebastian Weichwald (see https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us) and Erin Gabriel (erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk).

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

Specialist, POSM Demand Planning

Do you enjoy turning data into insights and forecasts that help a global business make better decisions? Are you motivated by working across markets and functions, balancing availability, inventory and commercial priorities?

We are looking for a Specialist, POSM Demand Planning to join our Global Merchandising & Supply Chain organisation in Copenhagen. In this role, you will support our global demand planning for Point of Sale Materials (POSM), covering areas such as packaging, accessories, displays, sellable items and services.

Your role

As our Demand Planning Specialist, you will help develop accurate, reliable and insight-driven item-level forecasts aligned with our commercial, marketing and inventory objectives.

You will work closely with clusters and global teams, with particular focus on new launches and item transitions. Through strong analysis and collaboration, you will help us improve availability while managing inventory and reducing the risk of obsolescence.

Your key responsibilities

In this role, you will:

• 
Support and execute the global POSM demand planning process, ensuring forecasts are delivered according to agreed timelines and standards.

• 
Consolidate and validate forecasts across clusters, ensuring strong data quality and timely cross-functional input.

• 
Develop item-level forecasts across packaging, accessories, displays and sellable POSM.

• 
Maintain statistical baseline forecasts using demand history, market intelligence, marketing plans, sell-in signals and lifecycle changes.

• 
Monitor forecast accuracy and bias, identify key demand drivers and conduct root-cause analyses to recommend corrective actions.

• 
Translate planning and performance data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations.

• 
Partner with Marketing, Clusters, Supply Planning and Procurement to build reliable forecasts for new launches and SKU transitions.

• 
Support phase-in and phase-out planning and proactively identify potential excess inventory, shortages and obsolescence risks.

• 
Work closely with clusters and global functions to align demand plans with commercial calendars, marketing campaigns, inventory targets and supply constraints.

• 
Contribute to improvements in planning processes, data and systems, helping strengthen planning quality, efficiency and inventory outcomes.

What we’re looking for

You are analytical and comfortable working with data, but equally confident turning numbers into a clear story for stakeholders. You enjoy collaborating across functions and markets, challenging assumptions constructively and taking ownership when something needs to move forward.

We imagine that you bring:

• 
1–3 years of relevant experience within Demand Planning, Supply Planning and/or Merchandise Planning.

• 
A relevant educational background in areas such as Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Finance & Economics or International Business, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 
Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

• 
Practical experience with forecasting, statistical modelling and root-cause analysis.

• 
An understanding of end-to-end supply chain and inventory trade-offs.

• 
Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.

• 
The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively across functions.

• 
A curious, proactive and solution-oriented mindset.

• 
Strong skills in Excel and PowerPoint.

• 
Experience with Logility or a similar demand planning system, and/or Aptos or another allocation system.

• 
Knowledge of Power BI, Power Query or QlikView is considered an advantage.

• 
Fluency in English.

Experience from retail, fashion or FMCG, as well as working in a global organisation across multiple markets or clusters, would be an advantage
